LESSON: PLAY SIMPLE

Grade: PP1
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PERFORMANCE
Topic 9.3: Play simple

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Play simple. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which game do you musical leaner should be able to: various electronic gadgets like playing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. listen and perform music for • Perform simple music from enjoyment various ICT devices
2. appreciate self and other’s • Coordinate parts of the body as performed music. they play music from various ICT devices • Observe safety as they use, operate and store electronic gadgets

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PLAY SIMPLE
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Play simple helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: PLAY SIMPLE
Study Play simple like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Listen and perform music for • Perform simple music from enjoyment various ICT devices

What this means
In this part you learn to listen and perform music for • Perform simple music from enjoyment various ICT devices. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: listen and perform music for • Perform simple music from enjoyment various ICT devices.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Play simple” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can listen and perform music for • Perform simple music from enjoyment various ICT devices. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate self and other’s • Coordinate parts of the body as performed music. they play music from various ICT devices • Observe safety as they use, operate and store electronic gadgets

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate self and other’s • Coordinate parts of the body as performed music. they play music from various ICT devices • Observe safety as they use, operate and store electronic gadgets. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate self and other’s • Coordinate parts of the body as performed music. they play music from various ICT devices • Observe safety as they use, operate and store electronic gadgets.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Play simple in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate self and other’s • Coordinate parts of the body as performed music. they play music from various ICT devices • Observe safety as they use, operate and store electronic gadgets. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Play simple is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Play simple” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: listen and perform music for • Perform simple music from enjoyment various ICT devices)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Play simple in your own words. (skill: appreciate self and other’s • Coordinate parts of the body as performed music. they play music from various ICT devices • Observe safety as they use, operate and store electronic gadgets)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Play simple to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: listen and perform music for • Perform simple music from enjoyment various ICT devices.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate self and other’s • Coordinate parts of the body as performed music. they play music from various ICT devices • Observe safety as they use, operate and store electronic gadgets.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Play simple from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Play simple: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Play simple?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which game do you musical leaner should be able to: various electronic gadgets like playing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Play simple means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: listen and perform music for • Perform simple music from enjoyment various ICT devices.
5. Be able to: appreciate self and other’s • Coordinate parts of the body as performed music. they play music from various ICT devices • Observe safety as they use, operate and store electronic gadgets.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
